title.narrative: Hygiene promotion (Awareness)

description.narrative: Hygiene promotion (Awareness)

title.narrative: WSH-I6 - Number of people reached with hygiene promotion/awareness raising activities

description.narrative: Under this output, activities are implemented in both Darfur and Gedaref and it includes:Conduct hygiene promotion activities (including home visits, FDG, and training of community hygiene promoters) on market days and using radio messaging to ensure reaching large numbers of people, Conduct Sanitation and Hygiene campaigns to reduce disease outbreaks in high-risk contexts

comment.narrative: Conduct hygiene promotion activity, training of community hygiene promoters in Al Manara IPDs camp in Ad Du'ayn, East Darfur

In Q2, GPA in Gedaref held 21 FGDs and 175 home visits reaching 700 people including PwDs, while NaHA in South Darfur trained 20 community hygiene promoters and delivered cholera-prevention messages through home visits, posters, and mobile loudspeakers. In Q3, ZOA in South Darfur continued cholera‑focused hygiene promotion; East Darfur supported awareness through renting 18 loudspeakers for mobile messaging; and GPA in Gedaref conducted further home visits, FGDs, and cleaning campaigns. In Q4, ZOA in South Darfur implemented hygiene promotion through home visits, FGDs, radio messaging, and training 22 and 36 promoters on safe latrine disposal and cholera prevention; North Darfur carried out two hygiene campaigns and one training for 30 promoters; and GPA in Gedaref continued hygiene promotion through home visits, FGDs, and cleaning activities.

title.narrative: Hygiene promotion

description.narrative: Hygiene promotion

title.narrative: WSH-I1 - Number of people having regular access to soap to meet hygienic needs

description.narrative: Under this output activities are implemented in Darfur and it includes: Distribution and installation of handwashing equipment (including soap) to HHs, schools and health centers and Distribution of hygiene kits.

comment.narrative: Distribution of hygiene kit in An Gabo, East Darfur

Q1: South Darfur (Nyala South & North): ZOA conducted a hygiene promotion campaign on safe latrine disposal benefiting 440 HHs. NaHA conducted a cholera-focused hygiene campaign reaching 3,200 individuals. Gedaref: GPA distributed hygiene kits to returnees from Gezira through the crisis modifier, with beneficiary data obtained via HAC due to security constraints. East Darfur: Distributed 100 hygiene kits to internally displaced women in Al Dyaien rural. Q3: East Darfur: Formed and trained 90 WASH committee members in isolation centers and 30 mobilizers on personal hygiene under the cholera response. Distributed hygiene kits. Q4: South Darfur (Nyala Shamal & Janoub): Installed handwashing stations (with soap), distributed WASH NFIs, and conducted latrine desludging with soap, all under the cholera response. North Darfur: Distributed hygiene kits to 384 HHs.

description.narrative: Under this output 12 schools wll be suported 4 in Gedaref and 8 in Darfur through rehabilitation and/or construction of learning facilities (classrooms, offices, fencing, latrines etc.), construction/upgrading teachers housing, improve school water systems and entertainment facilities. Also, one school (2 class rooms) was contracted in Al-jerafa, in Almaza locality Gedaref as part of the top up from JR4.

comment.narrative: In Gedaref, Al Jerefat village a school Unit (2 class rooms & one office) and latrines were constructed. GPA has successfully implemented forum on the importance of Education in Kassab and Wad Daeef schools. GPA has implemented session on social mobilization for communities and advocacy in Kassab and Wad Zayed villages at locality of Al Gallabat Al Garbia.

In Q1, ZOA in Gedaref constructed and rehabilitated two schools. In Q2, NaHA in South Darfur handed over a 4‑unit female latrine block at Salman Alfarisi Elementary School, serving 500 female students and 21 teachers. In Q3, the same latrine block was formally handed over in South Darfur, while ZOA in Gedaref continued construction and rehabilitation of two schools. In Q4, ZOA rehabilitated one classroom and a library at Alrayan School and four classrooms plus two offices at Alfaroug School in Nyala North, provided safe drinking water to Al-Saadia Girls’ Primary School, and constructed a VIP school latrine at Alsahawa Primary in Nyala South. In North Darfur, ZOA rehabilitated two schools, including a classroom and three teachers’ offices at Kassab Girls’ Primary and Wad Daeef Boys’ Primary

title.narrative: FSC-I1 - Number of people provided with resources to protect and start rebuilding livelihood assets

description.narrative: These activities are planned only in North Darfur and they include the following:Strengthen existing community-based committees (e.g., farmer committees and animal producers, etc.) for improved production (provision of locally procured seeds, tools, potentially business grants), Provision of technical and in-kind support to vulnerable households (women farmers), Construction and supporting committees to operate seed banks, Support Income generating activities (IGAs) targeting vulnerable women, Formation/strengthening and training of VSLA groups, Support animal vaccination campaigns, Training of community animal health workers, providing them with necessary equipment and animal treatments, and Establishment of goat banks (provision of livestock)

comment.narrative: Q4: ND, construction of 1 seed bank and rehabilitation of other, Establishment of 2 IGAs, establishment of 15 goat banks, training of 35 CAHWs and provided them with animal drugs and equipment for treating of animal and conducted one campaign for animal treatment

title.narrative: Water Supply

description.narrative: Water Supply

title.narrative: WSH-I4 - Number of people having access to sufficient and safe water for domestic use

description.narrative: Under this output, activities are implemented in both Darfur and Gedaref and it includes: Construction of new/rehabilitation of existing non-functional water points (including hand pumps, boreholes and water yards), Formation and training of Water Resources Management Committees (WRMCs) in target areas for sustained O&M of water points, Support water quality supply chain. In addition, the construction of Al-Jerefat water treatment plant (slow sand filter) and Drilling of Abu Annga water well (27) in Gedaref locality were carried out as part of the top-up (carry over).

comment.narrative: In Q1, ZOA rehabilitated the Al Kanz village water station in Al Ghallabat Al Gharbia, benefiting 11,500 people including PwDs, while GPA rehabilitated three water sources with solar systems in Gezira for 8,939 IDPs (not counted under this output). In Q3, ZOA in South Darfur rehabilitated the Majok water pump station, and in Gedaref continued constructing a new borehole in Abu Al Naja expected to serve 5,000 people in Madinet Al Gedaref upon completion. In Q4, ZOA in South Darfur rehabilitated one mini‑water system and one water pump station, trained two WRMCs for sustainable O&M, and supported WES with incentives for 10 chlorinators to treat water during the cholera outbreak in Nyala Shamal and Janoub, while in Gedaref the construction of the new borehole in Abu Al Naja continued with the same expected reach of 5,000 individuals
The elevated tank has been successfully installed, and the distribution point been constructed and the pipeline from the water station to village is completed in Al Jerefat village in Gedaref.
